LESSON: COMMUNICATING MESSAGES

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Care for the 3.3 Managing waste By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners to 
Topic 3.3.2: Communicating messages

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Communicating messages. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMMUNICATING MESSAGES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Communicating messages helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: COMMUNICATING MESSAGES
Study Communicating messages like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create 

What this means
In this part you learn to use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create . You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create .
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Communicating messages” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Communicating messages is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Communicating messages” around your school. (skill: use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Communicating messages to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create .
3. Make one local Kenya example of Communicating messages from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Communicating messages: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Communicating messages?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Communicating messages means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use hand, print and managing waste electronic media to create .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
